name: Dhyān Yog
title: Path of Meditation
summary: The sixth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Dhyana Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the "Yoga of Meditation" and how to practise this Yoga. He discusses the role of action in preparing for Meditation, how performing duties in devotion purifies one's mind and heightens one's spiritual consciousness. He explains in detail the obstacles that one faces when trying to control their mind and the exact methods by which one can conquer their mind. He reveals how one can focus their mind on Paramatma and unite with the God.

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said: He who performs his bounden duty without depending on the fruits of his actions—he is a sannyasi and a yogi, not he who is without fire and without action.
verses.translation2: Lord Shri Krishna said: He who acts out of duty, without considering the consequences, is truly spiritual and a true ascetic; not he who merely observes rituals or shuns all action.

verses.translation: Do you, O Arjuna, know that Yoga is what they call renunciation; no one indeed becomes a Yogi who has not renounced their thoughts.
verses.translation2: O Arjuna, renunciation is indeed what is known as right action. No one can become spiritually enlightened who has not renounced all desires.

verses.translation: For a sage who wishes to attain to Yoga, action is said to be the means; for the same sage who has attained Yoga, inaction is said to be the means.
verses.translation2: For the sage who seeks the heights of spiritual meditation, practice is the only method, and when they have attained it, they must maintain themselves there through continual self-control.

verses.translation: When a person is not attached to the sense-objects or to actions, having renounced all thoughts, then they are said to have attained Yoga.
verses.translation2: When a man renounces even the thought of initiating action, and is not interested in sense objects or any results that may flow from his acts, then he truly understands spirituality.

verses.translation: One should raise oneself by one's own self alone; let not one lower oneself; for the self alone is one's own friend, and the self alone is one's own enemy.
verses.translation2: Let him seek liberation with the help of his Highest Self, and never disgrace his own Self. For that Self is his only friend; yet it can also be his enemy.

verses.translation: The Self is the friend of the self of him by whom the Self has been conquered; but to the unconquered self, this Self stands in the position of an enemy, like an external foe.
verses.translation2: To one who has conquered their lower nature with its help, the Self is a friend; but to one who has not done so, it is an enemy.

verses.translation: The Supreme Self of him who is self-controlled and peaceful remains balanced in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as in honor and dishonor.
verses.translation2: The Self of one who is self-controlled and has attained peace is equally unmoved by heat or cold, pleasure or pain, honor or dishonor.

verses.translation: The Yogi who is satisfied with the knowledge and wisdom of the Self, who has conquered the senses, and to whom a clod of earth, a piece of stone, and gold are all the same, is said to have attained Nirvikalpa Samadhi.
verses.translation2: He who desires nothing but wisdom and spiritual insight, who has conquered his senses, and who looks upon a lump of earth, a stone, and fine gold with the same eye, is a real saint.

verses.translation: He who is of the same mind towards the good-hearted, friends, enemies, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, the relatives, the righteous, and the unrighteous, excels.
verses.translation2: He looks impartially on all—lovers, friends, or foes; indifferent, hostile, alien, or relative; virtuous or sinful.

verses.translation: Let the yogi constantly strive to keep the mind steady, remaining in solitude, alone, with the body and mind controlled, and free from hope and greed.
verses.translation2: Let the student of spirituality try unceasingly to concentrate his mind; let him live in seclusion, absolutely alone, with his mind and personality controlled, free from desire and without possessions.

verses.translation: In a clean spot, having established a firm seat of his own, neither too high nor too low, made of cloth, skin, and kusha grass layered one over the other.
verses.translation2: Having chosen a holy place, let him sit in a firm posture on a seat that is neither too high nor too low, and cover it with a grass mat, a deer skin, and a cloth.

verses.translation: There, having made the mind one-pointed, with the actions of the mind and senses controlled, let him, seated on the seat, practice Yoga for the purification of the self.
verses.translation2: Seated thus, with his mind concentrated, his functions controlled, and his senses governed, let him practice meditation for the purification of his lower nature.

verses.translation: Let him firmly hold his body, head, and neck erect and still, gazing at the tip of his nose without looking around.
verses.translation2: Let him hold his body, head, and neck erect, motionless and steady; let him look fixedly at the tip of his nose, turning neither to the right nor to the left.

verses.translation: Serene-minded, fearless, firm in the vow of a Brahmachari, having controlled their mind, thinking of Me and balanced in mind, let them sit, having Me as their supreme goal.
verses.translation2: With peace in his heart and no fear, observing the vow of celibacy, with his mind controlled and fixed on Me, let the student lose himself in contemplation of Me.

verses.translation: Thus, always keeping the mind balanced, the yogi, with the mind controlled, attains the peace abiding in Me, culminating in liberation.
verses.translation2: Thus, keeping his mind always in communion with Me and subduing his thoughts, he shall attain that Peace which is Mine and will lead him to liberation at last.

verses.translation: Verily, Yoga is not possible for him who eats too much, nor for him who does not eat at all, nor for him who sleeps too much, nor for him who is always awake, O Arjuna.
verses.translation2: Meditation is not for him who eats too much, nor for him who eats not at all; not for him who is overly addicted to sleep, nor for him who is always awake.

verses.translation: Yoga becomes the destroyer of pain for him who is moderate in eating and recreation (such as walking, etc.), who exercises moderation in action, and who is moderate in sleep and wakefulness.
verses.translation2: But for him who regulates his food and recreation, who is balanced in action, in sleep, and in waking, it shall dispel all unhappiness.

verses.translation: When the perfectly controlled mind rests in the Self alone, free from longing for any of the objects of desire, then it is said, 'He is united'.
verses.translation2: When the mind is completely controlled, centered in the Self, and free from all earthly desires, then the man is truly spiritual.

verses.translation: As a lamp placed in a windless spot does not flicker, so is the Yogi of a controlled mind, who practices Yoga in the Self, compared.
verses.translation2: The wise man who has conquered his mind and is absorbed in the Self is like a lamp that does not flicker, as it stands sheltered from every wind.

verses.translation: When the mind, restrained by the practice of yoga, attains quietude, and when one sees the Self by the Self, they are satisfied in their own Self.
verses.translation2: There, where the whole of nature is seen in the light of the Self, where the person abides within their Self and is satisfied there, their functions restrained by their union with the Divine, the mind finds rest.

verses.translation: When he (the Yogi) feels that infinite bliss which can be grasped by the pure intellect and which transcends the senses, and is established therein, never moving away from the reality.
verses.translation2: When he enjoys the bliss that surpasses the senses and can only be grasped by the pure intellect, when he comes to rest within his highest self, he will never again stray from reality.

verses.translation: Having obtained it, he thinks there is no other gain superior to it; established in it, he is not moved even by heavy sorrow.
verses.translation2: Finding That, he will realize that there is no possession so precious. And once established there, no calamity can disturb him.

verses.translation: Let this be known by the name of Yoga, the severance from union with pain. This Yoga should be practiced with determination and with an undespairing mind.
verses.translation2: This inner severance from the affliction of misery is spirituality. It should be practiced with determination and with a heart that refuses to be depressed.

verses.translation: Abandoning unreservedly all desires born of Sankalpa (thought and imagination) and completely restraining the whole group of senses by the mind from all sides.
verses.translation2: Renouncing every desire that can be imagined, controlling the senses at every point through the power of the mind;

verses.translation: Little by little, let him attain steadiness of the intellect by holding it firmly; having made the mind establish itself in the Self, let him not think of anything else.
verses.translation2: Little by little, with the help of his reason controlled by fortitude, let him attain peace; and, fixing his mind on the Self, let him not think of anything else.

verses.translation: From whatever cause the restless and unsteady mind wanders away, let him restrain it from that and bring it under the control of the Self alone.
verses.translation2: When the volatile and wavering mind wanders, let him restrain it and bring it back to its allegiance to the Self.

verses.translation: Supreme Bliss indeed comes to this Yogi whose mind is made peaceful, whose passion is quelled, who has become Brahman, and who is free from sin.
verses.translation2: Supreme bliss is the lot of the sage whose mind attains peace, whose passions subside, who is without sin, and who becomes one with the Absolute.

verses.translation: The yogi, always engaging the mind thus (in the practice of yoga), is freed from sins and easily enjoys the infinite bliss of contact with Brahman (the Eternal).
verses.translation2: Thus, free from sin, abiding always in the Eternal, the saint enjoys, without effort, the bliss that flows from the realization of the Infinite.

verses.translation: With the mind harmonized by Yoga, he sees the Self abiding in all beings and all beings in the Self; he sees the same everywhere.
verses.translation2: He who experiences the unity of life sees his own Self in all beings, and all beings in his own Self, and looks upon everything with an impartial eye.

verses.translation: He who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, never becomes separated from Me, nor do I from him.
verses.translation2: He who sees Me in everything and everything in Me, I shall never forsake him, nor shall he lose Me.

verses.translation2: The sage who realizes the unity of life and who worships Me in all beings, lives in Me, no matter what their lot may be.

verses.translation: He who, through the likeness of the Self, O Arjuna, sees reality everywhere, be it pleasure or pain, is regarded as the highest Yogi.
verses.translation2: O Arjuna! He is the perfect saint who, having been taught by the likeness within himself, sees the same Self everywhere, regardless of whether the outer form be pleasurable or painful.

verses.translation: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, I do not see how this Yoga of equanimity, which you have taught me, can be maintained steadily, due to the restlessness of the mind."
verses.translation2: Arjuna said: I do not see how I can attain this state of equanimity which You have revealed, owing to the restlessness of my mind.

verses.translation2: My Lord! Verily, the mind is fickle and turbulent, obstinate, and strong; indeed, it is extremely difficult to control, like the wind.

verses.translation2: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Doubtless, O Mighty One, the mind is fickle and exceedingly difficult to restrain; however, O Son of Kunti, with practice and renunciation, it can be done.

verses.translation2: It is not possible to attain Self-Realization unless one knows how to control oneself; however, for one who, striving by the proper means, learns such control, it is possible.

verses.translation2: Arjuna asked: What of him who fails to control himself, whose mind falls from spiritual contemplation, yet retains his faith and does not attain perfection?

verses.translation: Fallen from both, does he not perish like a rent cloud, supportless, O mighty-armed one, deluded on the path of Brahman?
verses.translation2: Having failed in both, my Lord, is he without hope, like a riven cloud with no support, lost on the spiritual path?

verses.translation: O Krishna, please completely dispel this doubt of mine, for it is not possible for anyone but You to do so.
verses.translation2: My Lord! You are worthy to solve this doubt once and for all; there is no one else competent to do so, save Yourself.

verses.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "O Arjuna, neither in this world nor in the next will there be destruction for him; none, indeed, who does good, O my son, ever comes to grief."
verses.translation2: Lord Shri Krishna replied: My beloved child! There is no destruction for him, either in this world or the next. No evil fate awaits him who treads the path of righteousness.
verses.words: śhrī-bhagavān uvācha=the Supreme Lord said; pārtha=Arjun, the son of Pritha; na eva=never; iha=in this world; na=never; amutra=in the next world; vināśhaḥ=destruction; tasya=his; vidyate=exists; na=never; hi=certainly; kalyāṇa-kṛit=one who strives for God-realization; kaśhchit=anyone; durgatim=evil destination; tāta=my friend; gachchhati=goes

verses.translation: Having attained to the worlds of the righteous and having dwelt there for everlasting years, he who fell from Yoga is born in a house of the pure and wealthy.
verses.translation2: Having reached the worlds where the righteous dwell, and having remained there for many years, he who has strayed from the path of spirituality will be born again into the family of the pure, benevolent, and prosperous.
verses.words: prāpya=attain; puṇya-kṛitām=of the virtuous; lokān=abodes; uṣhitvā=after dwelling; śhāśhvatīḥ=many; samāḥ=ages; śhuchīnām=of the pious; śhrī-matām=of the prosperous; gehe=in the house; yoga-bhraṣhṭaḥ=the unsuccessful yogis; abhijāyate=take birth

verses.translation: Or he is born in a family of even the wisest of yogis; verily, such a birth is very difficult to obtain in this world.
verses.translation2: Or, he may be born in the family of wise sages, though such a birth is indeed very difficult to obtain.
verses.words: atha vā=else; yoginām=of those endowed with divine wisdom; eva=certainly; kule=in the family; bhavati=take birth; dhī-matām=of the wise; etat=this; hi=certainly; durlabha-taram=very rare; loke=in this world; janma=birth; yat=which; īdṛiśham=like this

verses.translation: Then he comes into contact with the knowledge acquired in his former body and strives even more for perfection, O Arjuna.
verses.translation2: Then, the experience acquired in his former life will revive, and with it, he will more eagerly strive for perfection than before.
verses.words: tatra=there; tam=that; buddhi-sanyogam=reawaken their wisdom; labhate=obtains; paurva-dehikam=from the previous lives; yatate=strives; cha=and; tataḥ=thereafter; bhūyaḥ=again; sansiddhau=for perfection; kuru-nandana=Arjun, descendant of the Kurus

verses.translation: By that same former practice, he is borne on in spite of himself. Even he who merely wishes to know Yoga goes beyond the Brahmanic word.
verses.translation2: Unconsciously, he will return to the practices of his old life; thus, one who strives to attain spiritual consciousness is certainly superior to one who merely talks about it.
verses.words: pūrva=past; abhyāsena=discipline; tena=by that; eva=certainly; hriyate=is attracted; hi=surely; avaśhaḥ=helplessly; api=although; saḥ=that person; jijñāsuḥ=inquisitive; api=even; yogasya=about yog; śhabda-brahma=fruitive portion of the Vedas; ativartate=transcends

verses.translation: But the Yogi who strives assiduously, purified of sins and perfected gradually over many births, reaches the highest goal.
verses.translation2: Then, after many lives of earnest striving and absolution of sins, the student of spirituality attains perfection and reaches the Supreme.
verses.words: prayatnāt=with great effort; yatamānaḥ=endeavoring; tu=and; yogī=a yogi; sanśhuddha=purified; kilbiṣhaḥ=from material desires; aneka=after many, many; janma=births; sansiddhaḥ=attain perfection; tataḥ=then; yāti=attains; parām=the highest; gatim=path

verses.translation: The yogi is thought to be superior to the ascetics, even superior to those who have knowledge obtained through the study of scriptures; he is also superior to men of action; therefore, be thou a yogi, O Arjuna.
verses.translation2: The wise person is superior to the ascetic, the scholar, and the man of action; therefore, be thou a wise person, O Arjuna!
verses.words: tapasvibhyaḥ=than the ascetics; adhikaḥ=superior; yogī=a yogi; jñānibhyaḥ=than the persons of learning; api=even; mataḥ=considered; adhikaḥ=superior; karmibhyaḥ=than the ritualistic performers; cha=and; adhikaḥ=superior; yogī=a yogi; tasmāt=therefore; yogī=a yogi; bhava=just become; arjuna=Arjun

verses.translation: And among all the Yogis, he who, full of faith and with his inner self merged in Me, worships Me is deemed by Me to be the most devoted.
verses.translation2: I look upon him as the best of mystics, who, full of faith, worships Me and abides in Me.
verses.words: yoginām=of all yogis; api=however; sarveṣhām=all types of; mat-gatena=absorbed in me (God); antaḥ=inner; ātmanā=with the mind; śhraddhā-vān=with great faith; bhajate=engage in devotion; yaḥ=who; mām=to me; saḥ=he; me=by me; yukta-tamaḥ=the highest yogi; mataḥ=is considered
